name: Amazon
summary: An online assessment, then an interview loop where each interviewer covers different skills and the Leadership Principles.

process.note: Amazon's SDE pages describe these steps and say to expect at least one system design question. Round counts and lengths are commonly reported, not official.

stages.name: Application
stages.detail: Apply online for a specific role and level.

stages.name: Online assessment
stages.detail: A timed online assessment, usually including coding, for many engineering roles.

stages.name: Phone screen
stages.detail: Some candidates have a phone or video screen with an engineer or recruiter before the loop.

stages.name: Interview loop
stages.detail: You meet several employees one by one, each assessing different skills. A Bar Raiser takes part. Candidates often report about an hour per round, mixing technical and Leadership Principle questions.
rounds: System design, at least one question

stages.name: Outcome
stages.detail: Amazon's SDE II page says to expect an outcome within five business days of the loop.

design.note: Amazon's own prep page says to expect at least one system design question and lists practicality, reliability and scalability among its goals.

values.title: Leadership Principles
values.summary: Amazon publishes 16 Leadership Principles and uses them in everyday decisions and in interviews. The names are Amazon's; the one-line readings are ours.

items.name: Customer Obsession
items.gist: Start from what the customer needs and work back from there.

items.name: Ownership
items.gist: Think long term and act for the whole company, not only your team.

items.name: Invent and Simplify
items.gist: Look for new ideas anywhere and keep making things simpler.

items.name: Are Right, A Lot
items.gist: Use sound judgement and actively test your own beliefs.

items.name: Learn and Be Curious
items.gist: Keep learning and explore new possibilities.

items.name: Hire and Develop the Best
items.gist: Raise the bar with each hire and coach people to grow.

items.name: Insist on the Highest Standards
items.gist: Keep raising quality and fix problems for good.

items.name: Think Big
items.gist: Set a bold direction and look for new ways to serve customers.

items.name: Bias for Action
items.gist: Move quickly on reversible decisions and take sensible risks.

items.name: Frugality
items.gist: Do more with less; constraints spark invention.

items.name: Earn Trust
items.gist: Listen, be candid and hold yourself to the same bar as others.

items.name: Dive Deep
items.gist: Stay close to the details and question numbers that look off.

items.name: Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit
items.gist: Challenge respectfully, then fully back the decision.

items.name: Deliver Results
items.gist: Focus on the inputs that matter and finish on time despite setbacks.

items.name: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer
items.gist: Make work safer, fairer and more fulfilling for people.

items.name: Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
items.gist: Consider the wider effects of your decisions on the world.

prompts.text: Describe a time you changed a plan because of what you learned about a customer's real need.
Tell a story where you disagreed with a decision, said so, and then committed to it.
Talk about a problem you only solved by digging into data or logs others had skimmed.
Share a time you delivered under a tight deadline. What did you trade off?
